text:
Alex: Customer reports SSE stream drops after ~30s when their client is slow to read. Partial events delivered, then connection closed. Repro with curl -N + slow reader. Server log shows EAGAIN then EPIPE. Any quick triage tips?

Priya: Which customer / region? Is this only behind their corp proxy or do we see it from a straight curl -> hosted API?

Alex: AcmeCorp PROD, us-west. I repro locally against hosted endpoint with a small script. Here are the log lines from the runtime: 

```
[2026-03-16T18:12:07Z] conn=abcd1234 write() -> 8192 bytes, ret=-1 errno=11 (EAGAIN)
[2026-03-16T18:12:07Z] conn=abcd1234 write() -> 0 bytes, client closed
[2026-03-16T18:12:07Z] conn=abcd1234 aborting connection; reason=socket_write_error EPIPE
```

Alex: The client repro I used: `curl -N -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream | pv -qL 20` (limits read to 20B/s). After ~25-35s the server logs the EAGAIN/EPIPE and the connection drops.

Sam: Two usual suspects: 1) upstream proxy (corporate) buffering and then killing the connection once their buffer limit hits; 2) our runtime doing a blocking write and not re-queueing on EAGAIN. Can you capture tcpdump or h2/nginx logs?

Jordan: Also check any CDN/nginx in front of us. If nginx proxy_buffering is on it will try to buffer the whole response; with slow consumers that can exhaust proxy buffers and trigger a close when the upstream stalls. Check for `X-Accel-Buffering` header or `proxy_buffering off`.

Maya: From the runtime perspective, we should never assume the socket will accept all bytes. Current code path occasionally does `send(fd, buf, len, 0)` and treats any non-full write as terminal. We should modify the loop to: mark conn as write-paused, push remaining bytes into per-conn ring buffer, install EPOLLOUT and resume when writable. Also handle EAGAIN and EINTR explicitly.

Sam: Quick mitigation customers can try: `curl --no-buffer -H "Accept: text/event-stream" ...` or use `--raw`. For corp proxies ask them to disable response buffering or increase buffer sizes. Also test from a network without corporate proxy to isolate.

Alex: I ran curl directly from my laptop to hosted and still repro'd (no corp proxy) but only when I artificially slowed the read. So that suggests our runtime also has a write-path bug.

Priya: Customer also mentioned seeing a spike in billing tokens for the request that failed. Could retries be happening which double-bill?

Sam: If the client reconnects and we replay, that could create multiple billing events. But more likely the client saw partial output and retried, which created a new session. We should check request IDs and billing logs for that timeframe.

Jordan: Data we need: tcpdump of the failing connection, runtime debug logs with conn id, nginx/edge proxy config, and a reproduction command from the customer (curl + pv or the exact SDK + version).

Alex: Repro steps I'm attaching for the team to run locally:

```
# run this to simulate a slow reader
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=test \
  | pv -qL 15
```

# On server side monitor logs
sudo tcpdump -i any host <your-ip> and port 443 -w slowreader.pcap

Maya: I'll open an eng-runtime PR to harden writes: non-blocking send, per-conn queue, EPOLLOUT resume, and a backpressure watermark that triggers a 503 fallback if queue exceeds X MB to avoid unbounded memory growth.

Sam: Jordan — can you validate whether edge nginx has `proxy_buffering on` for SSE routes? If so, turning it off or adding `X-Accel-Buffering: no` from our side is a quick test.

Jordan: On it. Also will add a check to alerts: repeated EAGAIN/EPIPE on a connection should generate a small signal for SRE to investigate.

Alex: For next steps I told the customer: 1) try direct connection without corp proxy; 2) run curl repro; 3) send us tcpdump + SDK version. I'll mark this P2 for now.

deploy-bot: New ticket created: #SUP-10234 assigned to eng-runtime (Maya) and eng-sre (Jordan).

Priya: Thanks — please paste any relevant logs/tarball in the ticket. :mag_right:

Maya: Will follow up with a small patch this week and share a canary build. If we reproduce internally I'll include a test in the streaming integration tests to simulate slow consumers.

Alex: Great. If anyone finds a quick config change we can recommend to customers, drop it here and I'll forward.

Sam: One last note — also verify `SO_SNDBUF` sizes and consider setting `TCP_NODELAY` for SSE sockets so small writes don't get coalesced into larger kernel buffers that increase latency for slow readers.

Alex: Thanks team.
